newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Plains fed cattle market at standstill - trade.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Plains fed cattle market at standstill - trade.

text.p: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle markets on Tuesday were at a standstill, with packer buyers and cattle owners $2.00 to $3.00 per cwt apart, feedlot sources said.

Bids on Tuesday at $66.00-$67.00 were passed by owners pricing cattle at $68.00 to mostly $69.00, with a few still at $70.00, sources said. Most of last week's sales were at $67.00 although some were reported last Wednesday at $68.00.
Cattle were seen trading Wednesday at $68.00 or more if beef prices strengthen further, sources said. Prices also could be buoyed by packers' relatively short-bought status.
Beef prices were rebounding amid strong retailer demand sparked by last week's steep price decline, sources said.

Beef prices on Tuesday were quoted up $0.58 to $1.13 per cwt on 170 fabricated loads sold, USDA said. Heavyweight choice beef was quoted up $1.13 at $103.39, a $1.60 gain since prices started rebounding on Friday.

In the Texas Panhandle/western Oklahoma area, 30,200 head were reported sold for the week to date, including 18,400 formulated cattle to be shipped this week. Kansas weekly movement was 6,700 head including 3,600 contracted or formulated cattle.
